content.text:
I'm identifying the 3x3 shape pattern with cells at (0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(2,2), then scanning the input grid for matching copies to locate their anchor positions.

I found copy B at anchor (-1,4), copy C at anchor (-1,10), copy D at (4,3), copy E at (5,8), and I'm now checking copy F near rows6-8 cols0-2, testing anchor (6,-1) since the observed cells don't align with a full in-bounds shape.

I confirm F matches anchor (6,-1), then verify G at rows8-10 cols5-7 matching anchor (8,5), and H at rows9-11 cols9-11 matching anchor (9,9). I'm now starting to check copy I at rows10-11 cols1-3.

After verifying all cells are accounted for across the grid, I shift every anchor down by 3: A moves to (3,0), B to (2,4), C to (2,10), D to (7,3), E to (8,8), F to (9,-1), G to (11,5), while H and I fall out of bounds. Now I'm starting to construct the resulting 12-row grid.

I'm finishing mapping out the remaining rows, tracking which columns are marked for rows 3 through 11 across each shape's cells.

content.text:
The shape looks like two cells side by side with one below-right, height 2, so it shifts down by 2. I'm scanning the input grid to locate where this pattern occurs — finding matches around row0 col4, row1 cols 8-9 with row2 col10, and another near row0 col12, row1 col15.

I keep finding more instances: row2 cols0,1 with row3 col2 giving anchor (2,0); row3 cols6,7 with row4 col8 giving anchor (3,6); row5 col0, cols4,5 with row6 col6 giving anchor (5,4). Then I work through the trickier clipped cases at edges — row0 col4 and col12 seem to come from anchors just off the top edge, and row1 col15 looks like an anchor whose other cells fall outside the grid, leaving only that single visible cell.

I continue mapping the bottom half of the grid the same way: pairs of adjacent cells plus a third cell one row down establish anchors at (8,10), (8,14), (9,0), (10,6), (12,11), (14,9), and (15,4), with row15 col0 again being an edge case where most of the shape is clipped off. Now I need to shift every anchor down two rows and draw each clipped shape into the output grid.

Continuing the mapping: (11,0),(11,1),(12,2); (12,6),(12,7),(13,8); (14,11),(14,12),(15,13); then the remaining points (14,9),(14,-2),(15,4) shift off the grid entirely, so I can drop those.

Now I'm assembling the full 16x16 grid row by row from all these filled coordinates, marking zeros where empty and placing the shifted values at their new positions across rows 0 through 15.
